title: The Optician
strapline: Which is clearer — one, or two? Read me the letters on the chart — and choose your favourite pair of specs.
intent: The optician is a community helper many children or their families visit, and playing it out — especially for children who wear glasses — helps everyone understand and value the people who look after our eyes.
The role play builds knowledge of how we care for our bodies and of the many different jobs that keep us healthy.
Reading eye charts, matching letters and shapes, and testing 'which is clearer' weaves in early literacy, matching and careful looking.
Choosing frames, taking measurements and fitting glasses grows fine-motor control, decision-making and mathematics — sizes, pairs, matching.
Caring for worried or unsure patients and explaining the test grows empathy and clear communication.
Real vocabulary and knowledge flow in — optician, glasses, eyes, chart, test, frames, clear, blurry.
implementation: Set up an optician's — an eye-test chart with letters, pictures or shapes, a tray of frames (real, lens-free), mirrors, a testing chair and an appointment book.
Take a patient's role so children run the test: 'Cover one eye and read me the top line — can you see it clearly, or is it a bit blurry?'
Model the caring, careful talk and the reason for it — why we test our eyes, how glasses help us see, that wearing glasses is a great thing.
Bring in early literacy and maths — read and match the letters and shapes on the chart, sort frames by size and colour, match pairs, take measurements.
Add appointment cards and prescription slips for real writing, and a mirror and frame display for the fun of choosing and fitting.
Celebrate the children who wear real glasses — invite them to be the experts — and welcome an optician visitor or eye-care stories if you can.
key_questions: Cover one eye and read me the top line — is it clear, or a bit blurry?
Which is clearer — one, or two?
Can you match this letter on the chart?
How shall we sort the frames — by size, or by colour?
Why do glasses help us see?
